ai.description: *Duttaphrynus wokhaensis* is a small toad reaching 35–40 mm. It is brown with dark dorsal mottling and a pale mid-dorsal stripe. Key features include a prominent, elongated parotoid gland and warty skin.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Duttaphrynus wokhaensis* is best distinguished by its distinctively elongated, narrow parotoid glands that are significantly longer than the width of the upper eyelid.
ai.habitat: *Duttaphrynus wokhaensis* inhabits subtropical broadleaf forests and hilly terrains in Northeast India, typically found at elevations between 1,000 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Duttaphrynus wokhaensis is primarily nocturnal, emerging after sunset to forage for small invertebrates amidst the leaf litter of its forest floor habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Duttaphrynus wokhaensis* reproduces via external fertilization in water, laying eggs in long, gelatinous strings. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season (June–August).
ai.distributionRemarks: *Duttaphrynus wokhaensis* is endemic to the Wokha district of Nagaland in Northeast India, occurring at elevations of approximately 1,200 meters within the Eastern Himalayas.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Duttaphrynus wokhaensis* consists of a series of short, pulsed notes with a low-frequency pitch, typically heard in riparian habitats.
